build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

exclude: not picture 60: its packed bytes end on the disk where picture 78's packed bytes begin, and the unpacker reads on to the end of its 4-sector window, so these are those bytes decoded with picture 60's value table (side 2's, this snapshot's). Nothing reads them

comments.text: Picture 60's header, read by start_picture ($0586): its area, columns 1 to 11 and pixel rows 16 to 99 (inside the picture window, which picture_window_open $12CF clears from pixel row 16 to 111); then five words counted from the picture's start ($CA00, where load_portrait $2631 unpacks it): the base frame at +$004A, channel 0's script at +$000E, channel 1's script at +$001E, channel 2's script at +$0037 and 0 for channel 3, which it does not use.

Channel 0's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 5 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 1 then 2, frame 1 then 15, frame 1 then 2, frame 2 then 3, frame 3 then 19. One pass takes 41 steps.

Channel 1's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 8 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 4 then 12, frame 5 then 15, frame 5 then 8, frame 6 then 2, frame 7 then 25, frame 5 then 15, frame 5 then 10, frame 5 then 5. One pass takes 92 steps.

Channel 2's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 6 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 4 then 25, frame 8 then 1, frame 9 then 5, frame 10 then 15, frame 10 then 3, frame 11 then 15. One pass takes 64 steps.

Picture 60's base frame, which start_picture draws by storing (draw_frame_store $064E): a run count of 0 to start, then one block from column 1, pixel row 16, with $06 as its escape byte. Its bytes go down each column and on to the top of the next until the area is full: 924 bitmap bytes, written with 26 runs (the escape byte, then a count and a value).

Frame 1 of picture 60, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 1, 2 and 3: a run count of 0 to start, then 7 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 12 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 2 of picture 60, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 4: a run count of 0 to start, then 10 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 18 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 3 of picture 60, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 5: a run count of 0 to start, then 9 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 24 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 4 of picture 60, named by channel 1's entry 1 and channel 2's entry 1: empty, a run count of 0 and the $FF that ends the frame, so draw_frame_xor ($0648) changes nothing and the entry only waits.

Frame 5 of picture 60, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entries 2, 3, 6, 7 and 8: a run count of 0 to start, then 9 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 12 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 2 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 6 of picture 60, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entry 4: a run count of 0 to start, then 8 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 16 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 2 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 7 of picture 60, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entry 5: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 8 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 8 of picture 60, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 2's entry 2: a run count of 0 to start, then 6 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 10 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 2 to 4. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 9 of picture 60, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 2's entry 3: a run count of 0 to start, then 3 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 10 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 10 of picture 60, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 2's entries 4 and 5: a run count of 0 to start, then 5 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 19 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 11 of picture 60, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 2's entry 6: a run count of 0 to start, then 7 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 16 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 2 to 5. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Picture 60's own packed bytes go on past the last byte the picture code reads ($CEFE): 18 more bytes, decoded from the stream up to where picture 78's packed bytes begin on the disk. Nothing reads them; they are $08 and then 17 zeros.
